title: Nanyue
capsule: Nanyue (南越) was founded in 204 BCE by Zhao Tuo, a former Qin general, who declared himself Martial King over the territories of modern Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, and northern Vietnam after the Qin collapse. At its greatest extent, following the annexation of Âu Lạc in 179 BCE, Nanyue extended suzerainty over neighboring polities including Minyue and Yelang, while its rulers styled themselves emperors internally even while accepting nominal Han vassalage. The kingdom blended Chinese commandery-county administration with indigenous Yue customs for five generations of rulers. In 112 BCE, Prime Minister Lü Jia assassinated King Zhao Xing and the Han emissaries negotiating full submission; Emperor Wu dispatched 100,000 troops in five columns, Panyu fell, and the territory was reorganized into seven Han commanderies, extinguishing Nanyue in 111 BCE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is reasonably well attested through Han dynasty records and archaeology, though the precise borders of suzerain zones (Yelang, Minyue) remain approximate.
